quizzes.title: Basics Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Introduction, Data Types & Variables, Operators & Conditional Statements, Loops, Array, Strings, Function.

questions.prompt: Which header do you include to use cout?
questions.explanation: <iostream> provides cin and cout. <stdio.h> is the C library for printf.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Assume the usual #include lines.)
questions.explanation: Dividing two ints drops the decimals (3). % gives the remainder (1). Casting one side to double gives 3.5.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Assume the usual #include lines.)
questions.explanation: The loop runs for i = 1, 2, 3 and prints each square: 1 4 9.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Assume the usual #include lines.)
questions.explanation: The string is now "Hello World" (11 characters). substr(0, 5) takes the first five.

questions.prompt: What is the index of the first element of an array in C++?
questions.explanation: Arrays start at index 0, so an array of size 3 has indexes 0, 1 and 2.

questions.prompt: Complete the call so the program prints 5.
questions.explanation: The function is named add, so add(2, 3) returns 5.

quizzes.title: Memory & Pointers Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Pointers & References, Static & Dynamic Memory.

questions.prompt: What does & do in int *p = &x; ?
questions.explanation: The address-of operator & gives the memory address, which a pointer can store.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Assume the usual #include lines.)
questions.explanation: *p = 25 writes through the pointer, so x itself becomes 25.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Assume the usual #include lines.)
questions.explanation: A reference parameter works on the original variable, so a changes from 5 to 6.

questions.prompt: What must you do with memory created with new?
options: Free it with delete (or use a smart pointer)
questions.explanation: Memory from new is not released automatically. Forgetting delete causes a memory leak.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Assume the usual #include lines.)
questions.explanation: p + 2 moves two elements forward, and * reads the value there: arr[2] is 30.

questions.prompt: Complete the line that creates an int on the heap.
questions.explanation: new allocates memory on the heap and returns a pointer to it.

quizzes.title: Structures & OOP Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Structures & Enums, Class & Object, Encapsulation & Abstraction, Inheritance, Polymorphism, Operator Overloading, Friend Function & Class.

questions.prompt: What is the default access level of members in a class?
questions.explanation: Members of a class are private unless you say otherwise. In a struct they are public by default.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Assume the usual #include lines.)
questions.explanation: Because sound() is virtual, the version of the real object (Dog) runs, even through an Animal reference.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Assume the usual #include lines.)
questions.explanation: Constructors run from base to derived (A then B). Destructors run in the opposite order (~B then ~A).

questions.prompt: What is operator overloading?
options: Using too many operators in one line
Replacing the compiler's operators for every type
Giving an operator a meaning for your own class
questions.explanation: You write a function such as operator+ so that a + b works for your own objects.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Assume the usual #include lines.)
questions.explanation: The first withdrawal works (100 - 30). The second is refused because 500 is more than the balance. Encapsulation protects the data.

questions.prompt: Complete the inheritance line so Dog can use name().
questions.explanation: public inheritance keeps the base class's public members public in the derived class.

quizzes.title: Advanced C++ Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Templates, Exception Handling, STL: vector, map & Algorithms, File Handling.

questions.prompt: What does template <typename T> let you do?
options: Write one function or class that works with many types
Create a class with no members
questions.explanation: T is a placeholder type. The compiler creates a real version for each type you use.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Assume the usual #include lines.)
questions.explanation: The same template works for int (9) and for double (2.5).

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Assume the usual #include lines.)
questions.explanation: The thrown error jumps to catch, then the program continues with the next line.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Assume the usual #include lines.)
questions.explanation: After sorting v is {1, 3, 4}. Then 0 is added at the end: first is 1, last is 0, and the size is 4.

questions.prompt: Which open mode adds to the end of a file and keeps the old content?
questions.explanation: ios::app (append) writes at the end. Opening with ios::out alone erases the old content.

questions.prompt: Complete the method that tells how many times key "b" is in the map (0 or 1).
questions.explanation: count(key) returns 1 if the key exists and 0 if it does not.
